title: Fleet topology scenario mapper & procurement sketch — Private/VPC
summary: Working mapper for multiple fleet topology permutations for Private/VPC deployments. Purpose: produce quick-turn procurement sketches, rack/power/network estimates, and region split scenarios to inform dedicated purchase windows and ops readiness.
body:
Context and goal:
- Customers are increasingly asking for predictable latency in Private/VPC deployments across regions. We need a compact tool-like spreadsheet (this doc) to map node counts, racks, power, and rough BOM cost under three distinct scenarios (Constrained, Growth, Peak-surge).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model mix selected for initial run: A100 80GB (training/large-run), H100 80GB (high-throughput), and L4 (edge inference).
- Typical runtime mix for Private: 60% generation workloads (latency-sensitive), 30% batched embeddings, 10% offline/async.
- Target sustained GPU utilization (useful work) = 55% for baseline, 70% for optimized (aggressive bin-packing), 40% for conservative (ops buffer).
- Average request sequence length = 120 tokens; average generation tokens per request = 150; effective tokens/sec per GPU depends on batch factor.
- Rack density: standard 4U GPU nodes (4x GPUs) per rack = 12 nodes per 42U rack (48 GPUs/rack) for dense configs.
- Power per GPU (avg): A100 80GB = 400W, H100 = 450W, L4 = 125W. PUE assumed = 1.35 (initial planning).
- Network: 100Gbps spine; per rack east-west >1Tbps aggregate recommended with 2x100Gb NICs per node for H100/A100 heavy racks.
- Spare buffer (hot spare GPUs) = 5% of total GPU count.
- Procurement lead times: A100/H100 = 10–14 weeks; L4 = 6–8 weeks.

Scenarios (high level):
1) Constrained (steady-state conservative ops): target 40% utilization target to prioritize headroom and easier scheduling.
2) Growth (baseline planning): 55% utilization, assume 12% qtr-on-qtr growth, plan 18-month runway.
3) Peak-surge (cost-optimized aggressive): 70% utilization with autoscaling and spillover to hosted; used for pricing & unit-econ comparison.

Example calculation block (text table):
- Workload target: sustained equivalent of 1M gen requests/day (avg seq 120 tokens, 150 gen tokens) => roughly 150M tokens/day.
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (approx): A100@batched config = 220 tokens/s, H100 = 320 tokens/s, L4 = 40 tokens/s.
- Tokens/hour per GPU: A100=792k, H100=1.15M, L4=144k.
- Useful hours/month per GPU = 720 (24x30) * utilization fraction.

Illustrative node math (Baseline scenario, Growth):
- Requirement: support 150M tokens/day = 1.736k tokens/sec sustained.
- If we standardize on H100 for gen: tokens/sec per GPU=320 -> GPUs required raw = ceil(1736/320)=6 GPUs (raw).
- Add buffer (5% hot spare) and overhead for batching inefficiencies (~15%) -> effective multiplier ~1.20 -> 6 *1.20 = 7.2 -> round up to 8 GPUs -> 2 nodes (4 GPUs/node).
- For real customer fleets we don't colocate all workloads on one region/model. Multiply by concurrency and tail allowances; this small example shows why per-customer topologies vary significantly.

Regional split example (recommended starting split):
- US-WEST1: 50% of capacity (primary), EU-WEST1: 30% (data residency + latency), AP-SOUTHEAST1: 20% (APAC pilot).
- Use heterogeneous racks: mix H100-heavy racks in US-WEST for largest customers, A100 reserved for customers with long-sequence/transcoded models, L4 in APAC and edge-closer racks for cost-sensitive workloads.

Procurement sketch and BOM items (per 48-GPU rack nominal):
- 12 x 4GPU nodes (configured as 4x A100/H100 per node)
- Total GPUs: 48
- Estimated GPU cost: H100 (list est.) = $35k/GPU -> 48 * 35k = $1.68M
- Servers (chassis + CPU + DRAM + NVMe): ~ $18k per 4-GPU node -> 12 * 18k = $216k
- Switching (Top-of-Rack + aggregation): 2x 32/100Gb leaf switches + 2x 400Gb uplink ports -> $60k
- Power distribution + PDUs + cabling -> $15k
- Rack, KVM, rail kit -> $6k
- Cooling delta (row-level budget) -> estimate incremental OPEX multi-year, initial capex estimate included in facility uplift: $25k
- Rack-level total capex estimate (gpu+servers+network+rack) -> ~$2.0M (rounded).

Power and cooling quick calc (per 48-GPU rack):
- GPU power sum (H100): 48 * 450W = 21,600W (21.6kW).
- Nodes/CPU/DRAM/GPU fans ~ additional 9kW -> raw rack draw ~30.6kW.
- With PUE 1.35 -> facility draw ~41.3kW.
- Ensure facility PDUs and UPS sizing support 50kW per rack planning headroom.

Utilization sensitivity grid (text):
- If utilization falls to 40% (conservative) -> effective capacity drops; for same throughput we need +37.5% additional GPUs.
- If we push to 70% (aggressive) -> we can reduce GPUs needed by ~20% vs baseline but increase risk of latency tail and slower scheduling.

Operations notes and constraints:
- Spare parts: maintain 2% of racks worth of spare nodes at region hubs for hot-swap to minimize RTO.
- Firmware/networking: test dual-topology NICs for RDMA fallback; lock firmware image across node fleet for safety.
- Maintenance windows should be model-aware: avoid rolling updates across racks that host primary production models simultaneously.
- Monitoring: tie per-GPU utilization to console alarms; add tracer for model variant fallbacks to hosted when queue depth exceeds threshold.

Next steps (action items):
- (Ethan) finalize per-region rack budget and push to procurement for soft quotes (due 2026-03-01).
- (Priya) run the same scenario using mixed-node density (8x GPUs 2U nodes) to compare rack/power tradeoffs (due 2026-02-22).
- (Marisol) validate lead-time assumptions with vendors and add updated lead times to the sheet (due 2026-02-28).
- (Liam) prototype a quick pivot spreadsheet (CSV) that accepts target tokens/day and outputs node/rack/region counts with cost and power (due 2026-02-20).

Questions / open issues:
- Should we treat A100 vs H100 price delta as deterministic or use a price band (we currently model list price only)?
- What is the canonical procurement approval path for multi-region purchases > $1M per rack? (Finance/Legal input needed).
- Do we standardize on 4x GPU nodes or consider pod-level: 8x GPU 2U nodes to reduce networking & PSU overhead?

Appendix - quick checks to replicate calculations in a sheet:
- Inputs: target_tokens_per_day, avg_tokens_per_request, tokens_per_gpu_sec_by_model, avg_utilization, gpu_power_watts, gpu_price, nodes_per_rack, gpus_per_node, pue.
- Derived: tokens_per_day_required -> tokens_per_sec -> GPUs_raw -> GPUs_with_overheads -> nodes_needed -> racks_needed -> capex_estimate -> power_draw_raw -> facility_power_draw.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a lightweight, human-readable mapper rather than a locked BOM. The goal is to converge to a recommended topology template for pilot Private customers and produce an initial procurement ask for budget review. Please comment inline on region split preference, preferred node density, and any vendor relationships we should prioritize.
